references.text: Describes the birth of Ishmael, son of Abram and Hagar, which is relevant for understanding the background of Ishmael's lineage mentioned in Genesis 25:12
Describes the events surrounding Hagar and Ishmael after they were sent away by Abraham, providing context for Ishmael's descendants
God promises Abraham that Ishmael will also become a great nation, which is directly relevant to understanding the significance of Ishmael's lineage
A parallel genealogy listing Ishmael's descendants, corresponding to the list in Genesis 25:13-16
Creates a theological contrast between the family histories of Ishmael and Isaac as parallel headings.
Confirms historically and theologically that Ishmael is one of Abraham's two sons.
Reinforces Hagar's identity as an Egyptian slave woman and mother of Abraham's son.
Adds a time element to Ishmael's birth, confirming his place in the family history.
Provides background for Hagar's role as a slave woman before Ishmael's birth.
Creates a theological contrast between Sarah as the mother of God's people and Hagar as the mother of Ishmael.
Provides context on how Hagar came into Abraham's household before Ishmael's birth.
Paul interprets the event concerning Hagar and Ishmael theologically as an allegory for two covenants.
Confirms Ishmael's place in Abraham's covenant through circumcision, even though he is not the promised heir.
Creates a theological contrast by confirming that Isaac, not Ishmael, is the chosen line of inheritance.
